intro: Content moderators on mac often struggle to keep policy documents and decision logs in one place. You can use Notion to create a central hub for your moderation guidelines, audit trails, and team communication. This guide shows you how to set up your workspace to handle high volumes of data without losing track of your daily tasks.
tldr: Use a central database to track moderation decisions and audit trails.
Keep your policy guidelines in a linked subpage for quick access during reviews.
Utilize keyboard shortcuts to speed up data entry in your Notion databases.
Connect your moderation dashboard to Notion using web embeds for a unified view.
Set up recurring templates for your daily reports to save time each morning.

blocks.text: Setting up your moderation dashboard in Notion

Your workspace needs to be fast. Start by creating a main database for your daily logs. Use the `/database` command to create a table. Add columns for Date, Content ID, Policy Category, and Decision Status. This structure helps you filter your work later. You can create a new entry for every ticket you process. This ensures you have a record for every decision made during your shift.

Moderation policies change often. Keep your documentation in a separate page within your workspace. Use the `/toggle` command to hide details under specific policy headers. This keeps your screen clean while you look for quick answers. You can link these pages directly into your main database. This allows you to open a policy while you are filling out a log entry.
Speed up your work with keyboard shortcuts

items: Use ⌘ + P to open the search bar and jump to any page in seconds.
Type / then the name of the block to add elements without using your mouse.
Use ⌘ + Shift + L to toggle dark mode if you work in low light environments.
Press ⌘ + N to create a new page instantly when a new incident occurs.
Use ⇧ + ? to view the full list of shortcuts inside the app.

blocks.text: When you have thousands of entries, databases can feel slow. Use the filter feature to hide old tickets. Click the Filter button in the top right of your database. Select the Status property and set it to In Progress. This keeps your view focused on current work. You can create different views for different team members or policy categories. This is better than one massive list.

If you need to move data from a CSV file into your Notion database, use the Import feature. Go to the Sidebar, click Import, and select CSV. This is the fastest way to bring in bulk logs from your main moderation platform.
blocks.title: Bulk data management

blocks.text: Content moderation is often a team effort. Use the @ mention feature to tag colleagues in comments. This notifies them immediately. You can also share specific pages with your lead for review. Set the permissions to Can comment so they can give feedback without editing your logs. This creates a clear trail of communication for every case.

faq.question: Can I use Notion to track my moderation queue?
faq.answer: Yes, you can build a database in Notion to track your queue. Use properties like Status, Priority, and Assigned To to manage your tasks. While it does not replace a dedicated moderation platform, it is excellent for logging decisions and keeping notes.

faq.question: Is it safe to store moderation logs in Notion?
faq.answer: Notion has security features like two-factor authentication. Always ensure you are not saving private user data or PII in your workspace. Check your company policy on data handling before moving information into any third-party app.

faq.question: How do I speed up Notion on my Mac?
faq.answer: Keep your workspace lean by archiving old pages. Use the desktop app instead of the browser for better performance. If the app feels slow, press ⌘ + R to reload it. Ensure you are running macOS 13 or later for the best compatibility.
